findings.claim: The entry page draws its timestamp in the browser's zone while every other moment in this area is resolved in the caller's Account.timezone. It is not the defect the review raised — nothing can throw and no second source contradicts it on that screen — but the spec never says which clock the entry page reads, so the answer was chosen by the implementation rather than decided.

witness.detail: specs/portal/01-home.md:114 REQ-01-010 — 'THE SYSTEM SHALL compute the personal half over the calendar month containing the caller's own today, resolved in Account.timezone, falling back to UTC when it is unset.' The contracts' §Screens Q3 row names the entry page's inputs as 'the entry id; the caller's role and project memberships' and says nothing about a zone. apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/news/[entryId]/page.tsx:188 builds `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { weekday, day, month, hour, minute })` with no timeZone option, so `occurredAt` is drawn in whatever zone the device is set to. A caller whose Account.timezone is America/Los_Angeles, reading on a laptop set to Europe/Warsaw, sees an entry's time in Warsaw while the home screen they arrived from resolved every date in Los Angeles.

findings.suggestedFix: Say which clock an entry page reads. If it is the caller's, the page needs the zone the feed now resolves and the fix is one argument; if it is the device's, that is defensible for a single timestamp with nothing to contradict it and should be written down once. Left unchanged this attempt because no finding asked for it and it would be unrequested surface in a diff already under review.

findings.symbol: Screens, states table, row "Q1 answered, no country"
findings.claim: The screen replaces the holidays list with PORTAL_MESSAGES.noCountry whenever no country is stated, while REQ-01-019 answers that same caller the global holidays. On an organization holding a global holiday the screen says no calendar reaches the caller while discarding rows the body carried. Carried forward unchanged from attempts 5 and 7; still true.

witness.detail: specs/portal/01-home.contracts.md:286 — 'Q1 answered, no country | The holidays list is replaced by PORTAL_MESSAGES.noCountry and a link to the profile.' specs/portal/01-home.md:175 — 'IF the caller's membership states no country, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer only the holidays whose countryCode is null.' Concrete case: an organization with one holiday whose countryCode is null, and a member whose membership states no country. GET .../portal/home answers holidays.countryCode null and holidays.upcoming carrying that row — TC-01-INT-07 asserts it. The screen draws the sentence in place of the list and never draws the row.

findings.suggestedFix: Either draw the sentence only when holidays.upcoming is empty, or stop answering global rows to a member with no country. The implementation follows the states table because that table is determinate; no case distinguishes the readings, because every case with no country also has no global holiday.

findings.claim: Five PORTAL_MESSAGES failure keys added in attempt 7 to close a CR-07 finding are not in the contracts' Error Messages table, which enumerates ten rows and no failure sentence. Carried forward.

witness.detail: specs/portal/01-home.contracts.md §Error Messages lists noProject, limitInvalid, cursorInvalid, groupsInvalid, settingsForbidden, feedEmptyTitle, feedEmptyBody, monthEmpty, requestsEmpty, noCountry — every one a success-path or refusal string. packages/validation/src/portal.ts additionally exports monthLoadFailed, feedLoadFailed, entryLoadFailed, settingsLoadFailed and settingsSaveFailed, added because a blocking finding required the six inline sentences to move into packages/validation on the convention every other area follows.

findings.suggestedFix: Either add the five failure rows, or state once that the table enumerates the messages the spec decides and that transport-failure text follows the shared convention unlisted. The second is probably right — no other area's spec lists its generic failure string — but it should be said rather than inferred.

findings.claim: A foreign Postgres holds port 5433 on this machine — the port every suite here is configured for. It produced failures that read as product defects in attempt 7 and still costs retries: the two client-participants cases it hits were flaky again this attempt.

witness.detail: `netstat -ano | grep ":5433" | grep LISTENING` returns two different PIDs. A direct pg connect from the host: 127.0.0.1:5433 fails authentication for devscribed/devscribed, while 127.0.0.1:5434 connects and answers current_user = devscribed — 5434 being the second port the project's own docker-compose publishes for the same container. `docker exec psql` succeeds either way, because it uses the container socket, which is why the container looks healthy. With apps/api/.env pointed at 5434: integration 20/20, targeted e2e exit 0 with 22 passed and 2 flaky (client-participants.spec.ts:167 and :248, the same pair, passing on retry).

findings.suggestedFix: Nothing in the product. The lever exists: apps/api/test/database-url.ts and e2e/environment.ts both honour TEST_DATABASE_URL and E2E_DATABASE_URL and both fall back to apps/api/.env, which is untracked and now names 5434. A person who wants 5433 back has to find what took it; nothing here killed it.

shardDecision: One child on the whole set, not two. The two findings are a single mechanism — an unresolvable Account.timezone reaching Intl without a fallback — and splitting them across an API writer and a web writer would have produced two guards where the defect is that a rule exists at some call sites and not others. The lead ran the diff sweep independently before dispatching and checked the child's list against its own, which is how portal-home.service.ts was cleared as already safe rather than assumed; and the lead proved the child's new integration case can fail by reverting the resolver and observing the RangeError, since a child may run no suite.
